newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ's Countrywide MD makes plea for fiscal prudence.
newsitem.headline: NZ's Countrywide MD makes plea for fiscal prudence.

text.p: Countrywide Bank Managing Director David Wolfenden on Monday urged any incoming coalition government to remain fiscally prudent.

Wolfenden, in a speech to the Institute of Chartered Accountants in Hastings, said it would be a tragedy if any new government was to place fiscal policy "at loggerheads" with monetary policy by implementing policies that led to greater government intervention, spending and debt.
New Zealand, he said, had probably the best monetary and fiscal policy frameworks of any country.
As a result, growth had averaged four percent a year since 1992 and unemployment had halved to six percent.

"This country's remarkable transformation was the result of policies that depoliticised money management by Parliament implementing the Reserve Bank Act, which in turn has enabled price sensitivity to be managed within the two percent inflation band," Wolfenden said. -- Wellington Newsroom (64-4-4734746)
